entities.summary:
The Boeing Company is an American multinational aerospace and defense corporation founded in 1916 by William Boeing in Seattle, Washington. The world's largest aerospace manufacturer by revenue, Boeing's commercial aircraft dominate global aviation alongside Airbus, while its defense divisions produce fighter jets, missiles, and space systems.

Boeing's early decades produced iconic aircraft including the B-17 Flying Fortress, which flew over Germany in WWII, and the 707 jet airliner (1958), which launched the jet age and fundamentally changed global travel. The 747 (1969), nicknamed the 'Queen of the Skies,' democratized intercontinental travel by reducing costs enough for middle-class families to fly internationally. Boeing's aerospace innovations — from early jet transport to the Space Shuttle's development — shaped both commercial aviation and the space age.

Boeing's 737 MAX crisis — two fatal crashes in 2018-2019 killing 346 people, caused by the MCAS flight control software failing and being inadequately disclosed — became the most scrutinized aviation safety scandal in history. The 737 MAX was grounded for 20 months. Investigations revealed Boeing had prioritized speed-to-market over safety, pressuring FAA regulators and withholding information. The crisis cost Boeing $20 billion, damaged trust in aviation regulators globally, and prompted comprehensive reforms in aircraft certification processes.
